territorial_scope.description: Applies within United States federal criminal jurisdiction where the conduct uses interstate or foreign commerce, and extends to conduct where the offender or the victim is a United States national.

evidence.quote: This section applies if the individual who has violated subsection (a) or the identifiable individual who is a victim of the violation of subsection (a) is a national of the United States

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends Title 18 to create a federal offense of producing or distributing, with reckless disregard and without consent, software- or AI-generated intimate depictions of identifiable individuals that use interstate commerce. Penalties: fine, up to 5 years' imprisonment, or both. No effective date is stated.
summary.long: The bill adds section 1802 to chapter 88 of Title 18 of the United States Code, titled Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2025. It makes it an offense for whoever, in circumstances involving interstate or foreign commerce, acts with reckless disregard to produce or distribute, or causes to be produced or distributed, a digital forgery of an identifiable individual without the individual's consent. The offense is punishable by fine, imprisonment for not more than 5 years, or both. A digital forgery is an intimate visual depiction created through software, machine learning, artificial intelligence or other computer-generated means that appears to a reasonable person to be authentic. Intimate depictions cover uncovered genitals, pubic area, anus or female nipple, bodily sexual fluids, and sexually explicit conduct. Consent must be affirmative, conscious, competent and voluntary, free from force, fraud, misrepresentation or coercion. Exceptions cover good-faith distributions to law enforcement, as part of legal proceedings, in medical education, diagnosis or treatment, and in reporting or investigating unlawful content or unsolicited conduct. Communications service providers are excluded for content provided by another information content provider, unless the provider recklessly distributes content in violation of the section. The section applies extraterritorially where the offender or the victim is a United States national. Section 2(b) adds a clerical table-of-sections entry, and section 3 provides a severability clause. The text states no effective date.

relations.note: Adds new section 1802 at the end of chapter 88 (Sec. 2(a)). Sec. 2(b) also amends the chapter 88 table of sections (clerical amendment).

notes: Text is the introduced bill, with no enrolled or later version. No legal_basis, implements, repeal or transposition relations are stated. Sections 2256 and 2510 are cited without naming their act. Section 1802(a) uses 'reckless disregard' while 1802(b)(2) exempts communications providers unless they 'recklessly distribute'; the text defines neither term. Sec. 3 is a severability clause and creates no relation.

events.note: The bill text contains no dated or datable events. It has no introduction, enactment, entry-into-force, application, phase-in, deadline, sunset or repeal date, and no effective-date provision. Sections 1-3 state no time periods. The registry's 'introduced' stage is not stated in the document, so no legislative-step event is coded.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff in the bill changes legal treatment of a person, entity or service. The only number in the operative text is the imprisonment maximum of 5 years in new 18 U.S.C. 1802(a), which is a penalty and is recorded under enforcement, not thresholds. The interstate commerce circumstance in 1802(c), the 'national of the United States' test in 1802(d) and the definitions in 1802(e) contain no numeric values.
